text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 6.3% today after Brent crude oil surged more than 4% on reports that the U.S. is deploying a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East, amid escalating tensions involving Iran and concerns over regional stability. As a major refiner, Marathon benefits when crude oil prices rise relative to the refined products it sells—higher input costs are more than offset by the premium refiners can capture, especially when geopolitical risk tightens global supply.

The timing also matters: refineries are running at 92.5% capacity, near full utilization, so the company has limited spare capacity to ramp up production if demand spikes. That means Marathon is well-positioned to profit if crude prices stay elevated and Middle East supply concerns persist, since it can't easily produce more barrels but can sell what it makes at higher margins.
